name: Halftone Printing
visualIdentity: Tone is made from consistently shaped dots whose size or density follows luminance. Limited ink separations, clear outlines and paper texture create a printed image. Keep the dot grid anchored to its artwork and inspect scaling for moiré and lost detail. The source explicitly describes this style.
suitableUses: Well suited to tonal imagery, illustrated narratives, product or editorial introductions, archival explainers and comic-print objects. Editorial grids can support reading order; toon-lit 3D forms can feed halftone shading. These are inferred fits from the stated treatments and combinations.
limitations: Text should remain crisp and separate from the dot screen. Avoid moiré, crawling dots, frequencies near the pixel grid, glossy reflections and smooth shading in the 3D hybrid. Scale carefully to protect detail. Chapter transitions may be unsuitable when the topic is short, a causal link would be obscured, or a cut breaks a continuous shot or loop.
palette: Suggested new-art palette: paper #F8EFD9 background, dark blue #253E56 foreground ink, and red #C25143 accent. These are optional suggestions, not canonical values; exact task, brand, reference and existing semantic colors take precedence. Keep inks discrete and limited; no gradients or added spot colors. Red is decorative only for text contrast (4.029:1); use blue on paper for text (9.642:1), then verify actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Keep dot spacing, angle, shape and local coordinates fixed; animate artwork and masks rather than randomizing the screen. Map source luminance to dot size or density and antialias edges. Video motion should be deterministic and seekable. Optional interactive HTML can use finite scroll progress for chapter or story states, with backward movement restoring prior states; provide readable static/reduced-motion states and keyboard/touch support. The motion patterns are optional and should be used only when supported by the scene.
audio: No fixed genre, tempo, voice or required audio layer is specified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied audio choices and assets. Keep speech clear, avoid clipping and competing vocals, and synchronize sound and picture.
assetRequirements: Use source imagery or artwork suitable for luminance separations; prepare masks and preserve clear outlines and paper texture. Suggested implementation uses Canvas 2D for deterministic drawing, optionally a custom Three.js shader for luminance-driven dots, and Python/Pillow or optional Node Sharp for preprocessing. For editorial HTML, keep real HTML type and provide alt text; the 3D hybrid needs an accessible canvas description and still fallback.
combinations: Use alone for tonal imagery. With style-019, place halftoned images in a fixed editorial grid while keeping text unhalftoned; keep the red ink to at most one emphasis per view. With style-060, use toon-lit 3D luminance to drive dots, retaining only paper, blue and red tokens and stable dot frequency. Chapter-transition or storytelling patterns are optional, only when narrative progression supports them.
productionApproach: Select visual rendering and motion methods for the style and action; keep each animated property under one owner. HyperFrames is the primary scene, timing, media/audio sync, validation and export pipeline; Remotion is allowed only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, with the reason recorded. Neither dictates visual construction. Build time-deterministic layers or baked assets and inspect representative frames and final output.
